Title: Agents cannot delete other work, stop foreign processes or leak private data

## For the human
- **What:** в orch-it появляются три защиты, которые останавливают настоящий вред от агента: удаление чужой рабочей папки (или удаление сквозь ссылку в другую папку), остановку процесса, который запустил не этот агент, и отправку личных данных в открытый репо; четвёртая, отправка в main без зелёных тестов, уже стоит как защита ветки на GitHub и только проверяется.
- **Goal:** агент в любом репо на любой машине (Windows, Linux, macOS) не может уничтожить чужую работу, убить чужой процесс или выложить личные данные владельца в открытый репо, ложные срабатывания не мешают обычной работе, а каждое срабатывание и каждый сбой самой защиты видны в хранилище событий.
- **Plan:** один сильный агент с помощниками, как в частях 1 и 2: защиты решают по самому объекту (настоящий путь на диске, настоящее дерево процессов, настоящая видимость репо), а не по списку слов команды; подключаются хуком Claude Code и хуком git в самом orch-it, так что следующие сессии в нём уже под защитой; каждая часть вливается через пулл-реквест, зелёный на Linux и Windows.
- **Result:** на таблице из 40+ команд удаления (разные оболочки, разные способы) каждая, задевающая рабочую папку или ведущая сквозь ссылку наружу, отказана, а 20+ безобидных похожих команд проходят, одинаково на Linux и Windows, с учётом того, различает ли диск регистр букв; убить процесс не из своего дерева нельзя ни одним из 15+ способов, свой — можно; отправка с личными данными (путь домашней папки, имя машины, токен, слово из личного списка, личная почта в авторе коммита) в открытый репо отказана во всех случаях таблицы, в закрытый проходит; случай вне названных: рабочая папка, зарегистрированная вне обычного места, защищена так же; в закрывающем комментарии — прогон проверки личных данных по всей истории orch-it и расход самой части.
- **Undo:** two-way door (новый код в новом репо; хуки снимаются одной строкой настроек); touches orch-it, каждую сессию, которая в нём работает, и каждую отправку из него на GitHub.

## For the agent

Weight: 9

Step: part 3 of the rebuild order (#387 resolution, comment 6398337229): "the four guards: worktree delete with the file system's own case rule, foreign process stop, private data in the public repo; push to main = branch protection". Waits on parts 0 and 2 (proposal comment 6398217461, row 3), so it is blocked by #394. Driver: one strong agent with helpers, the same form as #393 and #394: an Opus 5.5 high background session in the orch-it checkout, own worktree; the path resolution (decision 2) and the process ownership rule (decision 3) are the strong agent's own units; the scanner patterns, CLI and wiring may go to Sonnet 5.5 / Haiku 5.5 helpers. The old repo is read only as a source of cases, never copied (#387).

### Why now

orch-it has no guard at all today: no `.claude/settings.json` in the repo, no hooks in the user settings (read 2026-10-25 21:30), and the part 1 and part 2 sessions run there in `bypassPermissions`. The old layer's `permission_guard` is wired only in the old repo.

### Decided by the brain (with reasons)

1. **Guards judge the object, not the words.** Each guard resolves what the command would act on (the real path on disk, the real process tree, the real visibility of the remote repo) and decides on that. A list of command words stays only as the trigger that says "this command can delete / stop / push"; the verdict is read from the object. Reason: the old guards judged text, and 32 breaks came from it (a verb list misses `unlink` and `find -delete`, a folder-name pattern misses a worktree elsewhere, a text kill rule cannot tell own from foreign).
2. **Worktree delete** (`worktree_delete`; the strong agent's unit). Protected: every worktree of the repo from `git worktree list --porcelain` (the main checkout included) and the repo's common `.git` folder, wherever they sit on disk. A command is refused when it can delete or move (the trigger set below) and one of its targets, resolved, is a protected root, an ancestor of one, or a folder whose tree holds a link (symlink, junction) leading outside that tree. Resolving: the command's own `cd` / `pushd` / `Set-Location` / `popd` tracked, `~` and environment variables expanded, MSYS `/c/...` and WSL drive paths read as drive paths only on Windows, links followed, and names compared by the file system's own case rule, measured on that folder (two spellings of one path are the same entry or not), never by the OS name and never by lower-casing. The link walk stops at the first link found and has no entry cap. Trigger set, on every OS: `rm`, `rmdir`, `unlink`, `del`, `erase`, `rd`, `ri`, `Remove-Item`, `mv` / `move` / `Move-Item` / `ren` of a protected root, `find ... -delete` or `-exec rm`, `rsync --delete`, `robocopy /MIR` or `/PURGE`, `git worktree remove|move|prune`, and inside `python -c` / `node -e` bodies `rmtree`, `os.remove`, `os.rmdir`, `unlink`, `rmSync`, `rm(`; wrappers unwrapped on every OS (`bash|sh|zsh -c`, `env`, `sudo`, `nice`, `nohup`, `timeout`, `xargs`) and on Windows also `cmd /c`, `pwsh` / `powershell -Command`, `wsl`. Every other command passes. Reason: the class is "a command removes a worktree or reaches through a link", so the path decides; the incident behind the link walk was a delete that went through a junction into another checkout.
3. **Foreign process stop** (`foreign_process_stop`; the strong agent's unit). A process is own when one of three facts proves it: its environment carries this session's id (the variable is the setting `session_env_var`, default `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID`, which Claude Code gives every shell and child of a session and the PreToolUse hook's input names as `session_id`), or its parent chain, checked with each parent's start time earlier than its child's (so a reused pid never counts), reaches the session's agent process, or the store holds a `process` step started by this session with that pid and start time. Nothing proven is foreign. The environment fact is what survives Git Bash's dead parents (P225) and a detached child; subagents run inside their session's process, so a worker's processes are its ORCH session's own (P871), and another background session's are foreign. `stop` ends the own process with its whole tree, children first (P521, P905). A stop command (`kill`, `pkill`, `killall`, `taskkill`, `tskill`, `Stop-Process` / `spps`, `wmic ... delete|terminate`, `Invoke-CimMethod ... Terminate`, `xargs kill`, `os.kill` / `process.kill` in a `-c` / `-e` body) is refused when any process it would stop is not own; a name or pattern target (`taskkill /IM`, `pkill -f`, `killall`) is resolved against the live process list, and one foreign match refuses the whole command. A target the guard cannot resolve (a variable, `$(...)`, a computed pid) is refused with the way: `python -m orch_it stop <pid>`, which applies the same rule at run time and stops the own process with its tree. Process facts come from `psutil` (one cross-platform reading on Windows, Linux and macOS, #378); it becomes orch-it's first runtime dependency. Reason: own versus foreign is a fact of the process tree, not of the command text.
4. **Private data in a public repo** (`private_data_public`). A git `pre-push` hook, so every route of a push is covered (agent, human, any tool). When the remote's repo is public (read from the GitHub API at push time; unknown or unreachable counts as public), every commit being pushed that the remote lacks is scanned: added lines, file paths, the commit message, author and committer name and email. Private, measured on the machine at push time: the home folder in every spelling of every OS, the host name; secrets by their published shapes (GitHub `ghp_` / `gho_` / `ghs_` / `ghu_` / `github_pat_`, Anthropic `sk-ant-`, OpenAI `sk-`, AWS `AKIA`, a private key block); an email that is neither a GitHub `noreply` address nor the account's public profile email; and each word of the per-machine private list (setting `private_words_file`, default `private_words.txt` in orch-it's data folder of #393 decision 3; a missing file is an empty list, not a refusal). The bare OS user name is not a pattern: generic names (`user`, `admin`) refuse half of all text, and the home path catches the real leak. A hit refuses the push and names file, line and kind, never the value; `guard.fired` carries the kind and location, never the value. The same scanner, with the machine-independent shapes only (secrets, home-path forms of any user, non-noreply emails), runs as a step of the required `linux` job over the pull request's commits, so a push from a machine without the hook still cannot reach `main`. Reason: the hook stops the leak before it is public; the job catches the machine that has no hook; reading the patterns at run time removes the hand-written file the old guard needed (#383 pattern 11).
5. **Push to main without green tests** (`main_push_no_green`): already held by `main`'s branch protection (part 0, #392), which GitHub enforces for every client. This part adds no hook for it; `python -m orch_it guards status` reads the protection and reports, as one `check` event each (`branch_protection`, `hooks_path`, `guard_install`): required checks present, strict, admins enforced, force push and deletion off, the pre-push hook and the Claude Code hook installed. Part 8's installer calls the same command in a target repo.
6. **Wiring.** One entry point per hook: `python -m orch_it hook pre-tool-use` (Claude Code PreToolUse, matched to the Bash and PowerShell tools, reading the hook's JSON from stdin, refusing with the guard's reason and the way) and `python -m orch_it hook pre-push`. `python -m orch_it guards install` sets `core.hooksPath` to the repo's tracked hooks folder and refuses, naming it, when another `core.hooksPath` is already set (S09-041); it never overwrites. orch-it's own tracked `.claude/settings.json` wires the PreToolUse hook, so every later session in orch-it, this part's own from its first merged unit, runs under the guards.
7. **Every verdict is an event.** Each deny and each pass of a triggered command writes `guard.fired` through part 1's writer API (a command that no trigger matches writes nothing); a guard that crashes lets the command through and writes `error.raised` with `failed_open: true` and the exception's code. Reason for failing open: a crashed guard that blocks every command stops all work in every repo, the "breaks at any sneeze" pain of the map; the event makes the crash visible and countable. `guard.reversed` is written by `python -m orch_it guards reverse <event id>` when a human or the brain marks a deny as false, so false fires are counted from the store, never from memory. The named query `guard-fires` lists, per guard and per week, denies, passes, reversals and failed-open errors.
8. **Record**: `GLOSSARY.md` gains only this part's words (guard, protected root, own process, private data, false fire); `docs/adr/0003` holds decisions 1, 3 and 7 (judging by the object, the process-tree ownership, failing open with an event: each surprising or costly to undo).

### Acceptance

| row | check | pass |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | worktree delete, both jobs | a table of at least 40 delete or move commands across `bash`, `sh -c`, `cmd /c` and `pwsh -Command` (the Windows-only wrappers in the `windows` job), each aimed at a protected root, an ancestor of one, or a folder holding a link outward, the past gaps among them (`cmd /c rmdir /s`, the same delete through `python -c`, `git worktree remove --force` on a worktree holding a junction): 100 % refused; at least 20 look-alike commands, the past false fires among them (`rm -r` of the agent's own scratch folder, `mklink /J` and `ln -s` creating a link, `.remove(` on a list, Lua `table.remove`, a delete word inside a string and inside a heredoc, `rm` of a file inside a worktree, `ls` of a root, `git worktree list`): 100 % pass |
| 2 | case rule, both jobs | on the `linux` job (case-sensitive) a worktree `Wt` and a plain folder `wt` side by side: deleting `wt` passes, deleting `Wt` is refused; on the `windows` job (case-insensitive) deleting `WT` for a worktree `wt` is refused; the verdict comes from the measured rule, shown by a test that fakes the opposite rule on the same OS and gets the opposite verdict |
| 3 | links, both jobs | a folder holding a symlink (and on Windows a junction) to another worktree: deleting the folder is refused; a folder holding a link that points inside itself passes; a tree of 10,000 entries with one link at the end is walked to the link |
| 4 | outside case: a worktree outside the usual folder | a worktree added with `git worktree add` at a path outside `.claude/worktrees` (another drive or temp folder) is protected exactly as one inside it, by rows 1-3's same commands |
| 5 | foreign process stop, both jobs | at least 15 stop forms (each command of decision 3, by pid, by name and by pattern) against a process started outside the test's session tree: 100 % refused, and the process is still alive after; the same forms against a child of the session: stopped; a child whose shell parent has exited (on the `windows` job through Git Bash, P225) and a detached child are still own and stopped; a process of another session (a different `session_env_var` value) is refused even when started by the same user from the same folder (P947); a reused pid (a foreign process whose start time is earlier than the recorded one) is refused; `stop` on a wrapper whose child holds a pipe leaves 0 processes of that tree (P521, P905); a wait on an own process (`wait`, `Wait-Process`, P974) is never refused |
| 6 | private data, both jobs | a throwaway bare repo marked public and one marked private: pushes carrying each kind of decision 4 (home path in each listed spelling, host name, each secret shape, a non-noreply author email, a private-list word, each of them in content, in a file path and in a commit message): 100 % refused to the public one with file, line and kind and no value in the message or the event; the same pushes to the private one pass; a clean push to the public one passes; visibility unreadable is refused |
| 7 | the job's scan | a pull request fixture whose commit holds a fake token and a home-folder path fails the `linux` job's scan step; a clean one passes |
| 8 | orch-it's whole history | the scanner run over every commit of orch-it's `main`; its hits (or `0`) posted in the closing comment, each with commit, kind and location, never the value |
| 9 | wiring and status | after `guards install` in a fresh clone, a `rm -rf` of a worktree through the Claude Code hook is refused and a push of a leaked path is refused; `guards install` with another `core.hooksPath` set refuses and leaves it unchanged; `guards status` on orch-it reports all six facts of decision 5 as `check` events; orch-it's `.claude/settings.json` wires the hook and this part's later units run under it |
| 10 | events | every row above writes its `guard.fired` events with guard, verdict and rule; a guard forced to raise lets the command pass and writes `error.raised` with `failed_open: true`; `guards reverse` writes `guard.reversed`; `guard-fires` over the test store shows the counts the tests wrote |
| 11 | how it lands | every unit a pull request to orch-it merged green on `linux` and `windows`; each diff reviewed on the Standards, Spec and edge-input axes (#381) with findings and fixes counted; report lines `tdd`, `codebase-design`, `domain-modeling` per the skill table; `session-cost` over this part's own sessions (dollars, % week, tokens per session and model, minutes) in the closing comment |

Outside case: a worktree registered outside `.claude/worktrees` (row 4): every named case sits in the usual folder, and a guard that finds worktrees by folder name (the old one, S09-007) leaves this one open to `rm -rf`.
Same object: Claude Code's own permission rules (`.claude/settings.json` `permissions.deny`) act on the same tool calls before the hook: this part adds no deny rule, so the two never disagree, and a user's own deny rules keep working. Git's `core.hooksPath` may already be set by the repo's owner or another tool: `guards install` refuses rather than overwrites (row 9). `main`'s branch protection (part 0, #392) is only read here. Part 2's `tests run` starts and stops its own test processes: they are children of the running session, so they are own and `stop` reaches them; part 2's bound kill runs inside its own code, not through a shell command, so the hook never sees it. Part 1's store and closed sets are owned by part 1: this part writes only kinds and codes already there; a new code goes into the closed-set file and `docs/events.md` in the same change, under part 1's agreement test. Part 2's session writes in orch-it until #394 closes; this part starts after that, so orch-it never has two writers at once.
Not in this ticket: stopping processes left running after a session ends (the launcher, part 6); the periodic check that opens a ticket per failed pattern and stops launches in a repo whose protection is red (pipeline model `:222-227`, parts 4 to 6, which call `guards status`); protecting a private repo's data in a test copy (#378: decided when the other repos are rebuilt); the removed red lines of the old guard (bulk delete, the machine's system folders, the harness files, secrets on disk, console windows, destroying on GitHub: #378 area 9); installing the guards into target repos (part 8); a history rewrite of anything row 8 finds (the owner's decision).
